subject: Questions in using NonWorn algorithm and calculating SRI

messages.author: 3e45b9c6ee08acd5
messages.subject: Questions in using NonWorn algorithm and calculating SRI
parts:
Greetings!

First, I would like to express my gratitude to the developers and all contributors of GGIR, which benefited my works greatly.

I have a few questions regarding sleep detection in my current study design, which involves hip-worn actigraphy 24/7, except during sleep (the actigraph is removed before sleep and worn again after getting out of bed). NO sleep diary since we instructed participants not to wear while sleep.

  1. In my case, the report seems to have correctly detected most of the non-wear periods (which correspond to the sleep periodsv in this design), but there seems to be an issue on day 5, and the wake-up time looks a little odd. Did I miss any arguments or settings to address such issues? 


2. Since my study design does not include wearing the actigraph during sleep, I understand that calculating the Sleep Regularity Index might not be feasible based on the original protocol. However, it seems that GGIR might have a way of handling this missing data? I’ve read the relevant chapter in the BOOK and was wondering if I’m correct in this context. Could my manuscript still be valid for calculating SRI?

Here is my manuscript:
g.shell.GGIR(
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir="",
             outputdir="",
             #f0=f0, f1=f1,
             overwrite = TRUE, 
             sensor.location="hip",
             do.imp=FALSE, 
             idloc=2, 
             print.filename=TRUE,
             storefolderstructure=FALSE,

             # Part 1 parameters:
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600), 
             do.cal=TRUE, 
             do.enmo = TRUE, 
             do.anglez=TRUE, 
             chunksize=1, 
             printsummary=TRUE,

             # Part 2 parameters:
             strategy = 1, 
             maxdur = 20, 
             includedaycrit = 6, 
             M5L5res = 10, 
             winhr = c(5,10), 
             qwindow=c(0,8,21,24), 
             ilevels = c(), 
             iglevels = TRUE,
             mvpathreshold =c(69.1), 
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             params_247=TRUE,
             epochvalues2csv=TRUE,

             # Part 3 parameters:
             do.part3.pdf=TRUE,
             anglethreshold=5,
             timethreshold= 5, 
             ignorenonwear = FALSE,

             # Part 4 parameters:
             excludefirstlast = FALSE, 
             includenightcrit = 6, 
             do.visual = TRUE,
             HASIB.algo="ColeKripke1992",
             sleepwindowType="SPT",
             Sadeh_axis="Y",
             HASPT.algo = c("NotWorn","HorAngle"),
             HASPT.ignore.invalid = NA,
             cosinor=TRUE,
             sleepefficiency.metric =2,
             IVIS.activity.metric = 2,
             IVIS_acc_threshold = log(20),
             IVIS_per_daypair = TRUE,

             # Part 5 parameters:
             excludefirstlast.part5=FALSE,
             save.ms5rawlevels=FALSE,
             threshold.lig = c(47.4), 
             threshold.mod = c(69.1), 
             threshold.vig = c(258.7), 
             boutcriter = 0.8,      
             boutcriter.in = 0.9,   
             boutcriter.lig = 0.8, 
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, 
             boutdur.in = c(10,20,30), 
             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10), 
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),    
             timewindow = c("WW"),

             # Report generation
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE, dofirstpage = TRUE, visualreport_without_invalid=TRUE,
             viewingwindow=2)

Thanks in advance!!!
Yue

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions in using NonWorn algorithm and calculating SRI
parts:
Hi Yue,

Re. point 1: Could you share the milestone file from the subfolder meta/basic in the output folder?

Re. point 2: If I understand correctly the idea of SRI is to monitor regularity in sleep, so I doubt it is informative when applied to a dataset where participants are instructed to take of the accelerometer when sleeping. Furthermore, the algorithm was proposed for wrist worn data, while I am not sure it is informative for hip-worn data.

Best,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions in using NonWorn algorithm and calculating SRI
parts:
Hi Vincent

Thank you for your kindly reply.

To Re. point 1.
I have update the files as attechment.

To Re.point 2.
Certainly, calculating the SRI without wear Actigraph during sleep is not align with the original idea of SRI, even though GGIR can handle unbalanced data (“includenightcrit”), but likely not the complete absence of sleep (if I understand correctly). However, this current design is indeed unique, and I appreciate you bringing this to my attention. And, I did miss this information that ths SRI-argument is based on wrist-worn actigraph data. I am genuinely interested in exploring validity tests for hip-worn devices in future studies.

Looking forward to hear from you

Yue

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions in using NonWorn algorithm and calculating SRI
parts:
Hi Yue,

Sorry for the delay. I was able to replicate your problem and noticed that the QC plot from part 2 explains what is happening:

For most nights GGIR detects the night of nonwear as expected, but on day 5 the participant also does not seem to have worn the accelerometer twice during daytime. Next, GGIR then labels the time in between as nonwear, because of the build in assumption that wear surrounded by a lot of nonwear cannot be informative. See also the documentation on this.

I think the best solution is to ignore this day via the day/night inclusion criteria.

Best,

Vincent
